title: Running Total (Prefix Sum)
description: Given an array of numbers, return a new array where each element is the sum of all elements up to and including that index.
whatShouldHappen: Create a result array with the same length.
Set result[0] to nums[0].
For every subsequent index, set result[i] = result[i-1] + nums[i].
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: A prefix sum array stores cumulative totals so any range sum query [i..j] can be answered in O(1) as prefix[j] - prefix[i-1] — trading one O(n) build pass for fast queries.

title: Product Except Self
description: Given an array of numbers, return an array where each element is the product of all elements except the one at that index. Do not use division.
whatShouldHappen: Build a prefix products array where prefix[i] = product of all elements before index i.
Build a suffix products array where suffix[i] = product of all elements after index i.
For each index i, the answer is prefix[i] * suffix[i].
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Two passes — one left-to-right, one right-to-left — build prefix and suffix product arrays. Their product at each index gives the answer without division, in O(n) time.

title: Find Pivot Index
description: Given an array of integers nums, calculate the pivot index where the sum of all numbers strictly to the left equals the sum of all numbers strictly to the right. Return the leftmost pivot index, or -1 if none exists.
whatShouldHappen: Compute totalSum across all elements in nums.
Initialize leftSum = 0.
For each index i, rightSum is totalSum - leftSum - nums[i].
If leftSum === rightSum, return i immediately.
Otherwise, add nums[i] to leftSum and continue.
patternExplanation: Using totalSum and tracking leftSum enables evaluating rightSum in O(1) at each step, yielding an O(n) solution without allocating extra arrays.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals to k using prefix sum frequency map.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize prefixMap with {0: 1} to account for subarrays starting at index 0.
Maintain a running sum accumulator and a match count.
For each num, add to running sum.
If (sum - k) exists in map, add its frequency to match count.
Record or increment sum frequency in the map.
patternExplanation: If prefixSum[j] - prefixSum[i] = k, then the subarray between i and j sums to k. A hash map tracks frequencies of past prefix sums in O(n) time.

title: Range Sum Query
description: Given an integer array nums and a list of queries [left, right], calculate the sum of elements between indices left and right inclusive for each query using a prefix sum array in O(1) per query.
whatShouldHappen: Construct a prefix sum array of size nums.length + 1 where prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i].
For each query [l, r], the range sum is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l].
Return the array of answers for all queries.
patternExplanation: Precomputing the cumulative sum allows any arbitrary interval sum to be computed in O(1) time by taking the difference of two prefix entries.

title: Left and Right Sum Differences
description: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, return an array answer of the same length where answer[i] = |leftSum[i] - rightSum[i]|.
whatShouldHappen: Calculate the total sum of all elements in nums.
Initialize left = 0 and an answer array of length nums.length.
For each index i, compute right = total - left - nums[i].
Set answer[i] = Math.abs(left - right).
Add nums[i] to left and continue to the next element.
patternExplanation: Accumulating from left while subtracting from total provides both prefixes and suffixes in a single pass with O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Contiguous Array (Equal 0s and 1s)
description: Given a binary array nums, return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0 and 1.
whatShouldHappen: Transform the problem: treat 0 as -1 and 1 as +1.
Now the problem becomes finding the longest subarray with sum equal to 0.
Use a Map to store the earliest index where each running sum occurred, initialized with sum 0 at index -1.
Iterate through nums, updating running sum.
If running sum was seen before, compute current_index - previous_index and update maxLength.
Otherwise, record the earliest index of this running sum in the map.
patternExplanation: By treating 0 as -1, equal count of 0s and 1s becomes a sub-array sum of 0, solvable with prefix sum index tracking in O(n).

title: Continuous Subarray Sum
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if nums has a good subarray: a continuous subarray of length at least two whose elements sum up to a multiple of k.
whatShouldHappen: Maintain running sum modulo k: runningSum = (runningSum + nums[i]) % k.
If two prefix sums have the same remainder when divided by k, the subarray between them is divisible by k.
Use a Map to store remainder -> earliest index seen, initialized with remainder 0 at index -1.
If remainder seen before and current_index - earliest_index >= 2, return true.
If remainder not in map, store remainder -> current_index.
patternExplanation: If prefixSum[j] % k === prefixSum[i] % k, then sum(nums[i+1..j]) is a multiple of k.
